owner_user_id/owner_team_id are set on Detector but no model column or migration defines them, breaking all detector creates and silently no-op'ing updates. — WHAT: create() passes `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` to Detector.objects.create unconditionally (even when None) and update() assigns the same names to the instance, but I searched the codebase for `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` and found no Detector model column, no migration, and no other reference — only this file. WHY: if the Detector model lacks these columns, every detector creation raises FieldError/TypeError even when the client sends no owner (because the kwargs are always passed), and the update() path silently drops the values in save() so owner changes are lost without error. HOW: add `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` (nullable BigInteger fields) to the Detector model with a migration in src/sentry/workflow_engine/migrations/ (site to check: src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py), or remove the kwargs/assignments.

Serializer field `user_agent` never matches the spec's `userAgent` key, so all real browser reports are rejected with 422. — WHAT: the serializer declares `user_agent = serializers.CharField()`, but browser-generated `application/reports+json` report entries (the exact content type this parser and endpoint exist for) use the camelCase key `userAgent` per the W3C Reporting spec that the code's own comments cite, and DRF performs no snake_case/camelCase mapping on input. WHY: every real, spec-conformant browser report fails validation with 'user_agent: This field is required' and is rejected with 422, so the endpoint collects zero real-world data, defeating the PR's stated purpose of supporting both spec drafts. HOW: declare the field with the spec key: `user_agent = serializers.CharField(source="userAgent")` (or name it `userAgent`); validated_data keying downstream is unaffected since only browser_report["type"] is consumed.

Truthy .get() checks let age=0 and timestamp=0 be submitted together, breaking the intended field mutual exclusion. — WHAT: the age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators test truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")` / `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`) instead of key presence, and `timestamp` allows 0 via min_value=0. WHY: a report with `age=0` and `timestamp=0` passes both validators, violating the intended invariant that the two fields are mutually exclusive across the two spec drafts. HOW: check presence with `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`.

body must accept a list per the Reporting API spec; DictField rejects every real browser report with a 422. — WHAT: `body = serializers.DictField()` rejects the actual browser payload, because in both Reporting API specs cited in this file (working draft w3.org/TR/reporting-1 and editor's draft) each report's `body` is a JSON ARRAY of report objects (e.g. `["{\"csp-violation\": {...}}"`]`, `["{\"deprecation\": {...}}"]`), not an object, and the parser (BrowserReportsJSONParser) performs no transformation. WHY: every real browser report fails DictField validation ('Expected a dictionary of items instead got a list'), the endpoint returns 422 for the whole batch, and the endpoint's stated purpose of collecting real-world browser report data never works. HOW: since the code explicitly must support both specs (old CSP level-2 used an object body, the unified spec uses an array), use `body = serializers.JSONField()` (or a custom field accepting dict|list) instead of DictField.

The new awaited retryCount update inside the catch block can itself throw and abort the entire cron loop, skipping all remaining reminders. — WHAT: the new catch handler performs an awaited prisma.workflowReminder.update, and if that write throws (transient DB error, or P2025 if the row was concurrently deleted), the rejection propagates out of the catch, out of the per-reminder for loop, and out of the handler. WHY: the whole cron run aborts mid-batch — every remaining unscheduled SMS reminder is skipped for that run and res.json is never called; the previous catch (console.log only) could not throw, so this makes the error-handling path a new failure source for the entire loop. HOW: wrap the update in its own try/catch (or append .catch(log)) so a failed retry-count increment only logs and the loop continues to the next reminder.

The new retryCount > 1 delete branch is not scoped to method: SMS, so non-SMS WorkflowReminder rows would be hard-deleted by this SMS-only cron if they ever carry retryCount > 1. — WHAT: the second OR branch of the new deleteMany — { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } — has no method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, unlike its sibling branch and the rest of this SMS-only cron. WHY: the deletion scope is broader than the retry scope: any non-SMS WorkflowReminder row (e.g. EMAIL reminders, which have their own scheduler cron) reaching retryCount > 1 would be silently hard-deleted by the SMS cron — a data-loss landmine the moment another reminder method adopts the same retry pattern. HOW: hoist method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the top level of the where clause so both OR branches only apply to SMS reminders.

Handle errors from the catch-block update so a single record failure does not abort the entire cron run. — The catch-block awaited update at lines 190-197 can throw unhandled on P2025 or transient DB errors, aborting the whole cron loop and skipping all remaining reminders.

join() skips terminate() for all flusher processes when the deadline is exhausted instead of terminating them as before — WHAT: in the new per-process join() loop, `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the whole loop, so `process.terminate()` is never reached for the remaining processes. WHY: the old code always terminated the flusher process after the wait loop even when the deadline was exceeded; now, if next_step.join(timeout) consumes the whole timeout, no flusher process is explicitly terminated and a process still mid-Redis-flush keeps running (holding its Kafka producer connection) past shutdown until the daemon is reaped. HOW: wait on each process only while time remains, but always fall through to terminate() for every process (see improved code).

Dead _create_process_for_shard would double-spawn a flusher for the same shards because it never kills the existing process — WHAT: _create_process_for_shard (new in this PR) has no caller anywhere in src/sentry, and if it were ever invoked it calls _create_process_for_shards without killing the current process for that process_index first. WHY: _create_process_for_shards overwrites self.processes[process_index], so the old process keeps flushing the same shards in parallel (duplicate segments produced to Kafka) and becomes untracked — _ensure_processes_alive can no longer see or restart it. HOW: kill the existing process before recreating it (as _ensure_processes_alive does), or delete the dead method.

get_memory_info() is now invoked once per flusher process buffer instead of once, amplifying Redis memory-info fanout N-fold per submit when the memory guard is enabled — WHAT: submit() previously called get_memory_info() once on the single full-shard buffer; it now loops over self.buffers.values() and calls it once per per-process buffer (N calls). WHY: get_memory_info is backed by iter_cluster_memory_usage (cluster/node-level Redis memory accounting, per the import in buffer.py), so each of the N calls repeats the same cluster-wide memory scan — N-fold amplification of Redis INFO-style commands on every submitted message whenever spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage < 1.0, which is exactly the memory-pressure scenario the guard exists for. HOW: keep a reference to the original all-shards buffer (self.buffer = buffer) and call get_memory_info() on it once, restoring the old single-call semantics.

New TotalDocs() call in searchSupport.init races with the just-started event goroutine's BuildIndex map write because bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates the cache without cacheMu.RLock, a fatal concurrent map iteration/write crash. — WHAT: The added startup log line calls s.search.TotalDocs() (bleveBackend.TotalDocs, bleve.go:144-154) which ranges over b.cache without acquiring b.cacheMu.RLock, while searchSupport.init has already started the event goroutine three lines earlier whose handleEvent -> getOrCreateIndex -> BuildIndex path writes b.cache[key] under Lock. WHY: This PR introduces the first (and only) caller of TotalDocs in the codebase, and it executes at exactly the moment the event loop begins: any watch event for a namespace skipped by InitMinCount (small namespaces, the common case) triggers a full build whose final `b.cache[key] = idx` write can overlap the unlocked map iteration (stretched by per-index DocCount() calls), causing the Go runtime's fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' and crashing the whole process at startup; the pre-change whole-function lock in BuildIndex masked concurrent builds but never made the unlocked TotalDocs read safe. HOW: Add `b.cacheMu.RLock(); defer b.cacheMu.RUnlock()` at the top of bleveBackend.TotalDocs (bleve.go:144), and/or compute total docs before starting the event goroutine in searchSupport.init.
